<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/submitter-exclusion-note.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run

Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5dd856f40c141947b63709cab0db235088f829a9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 33e748faad6632e3a03d79a5c61549666f616bf5 && git checkout 33e748faad6632e3a03d79a5c61549666f616bf5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5dd856f40c141947b63709cab0db235088f829a9 a3f98b15e78aa7c9719969f9a4b8d19efccb0c5c && git checkout -B drift-repro 5dd856f40c141947b63709cab0db235088f829a9 && git merge --no-ff a3f98b15e78aa7c9719969f9a4b8d19efccb0c5c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5dd856f40c141947b63709cab0db235088f829a9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `a3f98b15e78aa7c9719969f9a4b8d19efccb0c5c`.

**Gates on this head:** 55 check-runs, 0 failed, 0 pending; `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` success; all ten `Test Core` shards success.

**Shape:**
- Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #35316` and `Fixes #34410`, both delivered in full; the #34410 warning half took the guide arm, which the order allows.
- `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` patch changeset. 371 changed lines including tests, within the soft ≤ 400.
- `Clause-②: no` holds: the body's `.d.ts` diff of a base build against a head build shows no new export, key or topic. The message ids reach no declaration (`TranslationBundle`), and `__noApproverNote` is an internal snapshot key, the `__flowLabel` precedent. `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- The `docs/audits/…/plugin-approvals.md` census moves by exactly the one new elevated `sys_approval_action` insert, 16 → 17.

**What I checked myself:**
- **Ruling holds (option B, 2026-11-17).** Both submitter refusals still throw before any write. Only their closing sentence changes, and only when `namesNoOneBut(pendingApprovers, submitter)` holds. `onEmptyApprovers` semantics are untouched: the note is set only inside the existing `slateSource = 'no_one'` branch.
- **Platform slot stays out of the remedy text.** `slateNamesAPerson` counts `platform_admin:*` as a person (`approver-address.ts:265-266`). A platform-admin slate therefore keeps the old refusal text and never gets the "an organization administrator must add a member" text. `noApproverWho` also filters the platform address out of `who`.
- **Existing notice path reused (point 2).** The submitter is told under the existing `approval.comment` topic, with a per-request `dedupKey`, audience the submitter only, and no actor. No new topic.
- **Timeline note.** It follows the shape of its two sibling notes: an `action: 'comment'` row with `actor_id: null`, the English sentence stored, and the reader's language overlaid in `localizeRoutingNotes`.
- **Corrected sentence.** `approvalSubmitterExcludedNoOne` no longer promises an override the submitter cannot use, and the change is made in all eleven locales. The four new ids are present in all eleven.
- **Tests pin the order's cases.** The no-one slate writes the note, sends one `approval.comment` to the submitter, and the refusal ends with the remedy, asserted with its full text. The override refusal names `position 'legal'`. CONTROL: with another approver on the slate, both old texts are kept and no notice goes out. The platform slot label is read both on the stored row and on the door. The two fixture updates follow from the new notice and note; neither one loosens a check.
- **Docs.** Both `approvals.mdx` paragraphs match the code: the solo-admin plus `excludeSubmitter` route opens on the no-one slate, and the `platform_admin` waits with no warning when no one holds standing.

**On the area's four points:**
1. **#34410 guide arm.** Accepted. The order offers it, and the body gives the reason in one line: `hasPlatformAdminStanding` does not answer the population question, and a second derivation is what its header forbids.
2. **`approval.comment` reuse.** Accepted. It is the order's preferred path.
3. **Four commits.** Accepted. There is one commit per card, plus a fixture follow-up and a census follow-up found by the post-commit runs. The branch policy forbids a force-push, and the body says so.
4. **ADR-0027 §14.** Confirmed as a mis-number. ADR-0027 is the metadata-authoring lifecycle with sections 1–9, and no approvals source cites a §14. The body already records this. Nothing in the diff contradicts ADR-0027 §6 (publish approvals) or the other ADRs the order lists.

**Notes (non-blocking):**
- The refusal's `code`/`status` are unchanged (`FORBIDDEN:` prefix). The new assertions pin the message only, and this PR adds no new refusal.
- The stored `pending_approver_labels` is English by design; the reader's language is served on the door.

Next: non-governed, so a4-W lands per area-lease.
